detail:
BrainFacts.org, drawing on the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) Diseases A–Z series, describes how narcolepsy research is organized in the United States. NINDS and other institutes of the National Institutes of Health conduct research into narcolepsy and other sleep disorders in laboratories at the NIH and support additional research through grants to major medical institutions across the country.

Within the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, the National Center on Sleep Disorders Research coordinates federal sleep research activities, supports training programs, and shares information with private and nonprofit groups. The research directions described in the source focus on the biology of sleep-wake control, including the role of hypocretin, the brain chemical that is low in type 1 narcolepsy, and on clarifying the genetic and environmental factors that may contribute to the disorder.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about narcolepsy research and clinical trials.
summary: BrainFacts.org, drawing on NINDS, describes NIH-led narcolepsy research conducted at NIH laboratories and funded at medical institutions nationwide, coordinated in part by the National Center on Sleep Disorders Research.
takeaways: research is led by NINDS and other NIH institutes, per the source
hypocretin biology is a central focus of the work described
research participation is optional; talk to your doctor about studies
title: Narcolepsy: how NIH research into sleep-wake control is organized
